name: Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Science
notes: Six courses. The department calls this the 'Earth and planetary sciences minor'; the University's official program list names it Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Science.
Intended for students interested in careers in earth resources, space research and administration.
ASTR 111 may count in the planetary group only if EESC 101 and EESC 201 have been taken - the planner cannot check that condition.
See the department's major/minor course overlap policy.

requirementGroups.label: Two introductory courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Required Courses. Two of the following: EESC 101: Introduction to Earth Sciences; EESC 201: Evolution of the Earth; ASTR 111: The Solar System and Its Origin; ASTR 142: Elementary Astrophysics

requirementGroups.label: Two earth science courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus two of the following (prerequisites in parenthesis): EESC 203: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy (EESC 101 and EESC 201); EESC 204: Earth Materials; EESC 206: Petrology (EESC 204); EESC 208: Structural Geology (EESC 101 and EESC 201); EESC 211: Nature's Fury; EESC 214: Earth Science and Data Analysis (MATH 161 and MATH 162 or equivalent); EESC 215: Seismology and Earth Structure (EESC 101 and EESC 201); EESC 253: Geodynamics

requirementGroups.label: Two planetary science courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus two of the following (prerequisites in parenthesis): ASTR 111: The Solar System and its Origin (may be used here if EESC 101 and EESC 201 have been taken); EESC 229: Designing Your Space Mission; EESC 254/ASTR 265: Planetary Interiors (MATH 165 and PHYS 113 or equivalent); EESC 255: Planetary Science; EESC 256: Paleomagnetism and Global Plate Tectonics; ASTR 233: Astrodynamics
